stories.h: EFCC charges visa agent over N62.5m Hajj fraud
stories.p: The EFCC's Ilorin office has arraigned a woman described as a visa agent in a Kwara High Court in Ilorin, accusing her of taking N62.5 million from intending Hajj pilgrims. She faces a seven-count charge, which she denied, and was granted N5 million bail, Punch and TVC News report. The case continues in December.

stories.h: NSCDC decorates 210 promoted officers in Enugu
stories.p: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Enugu State has decorated 210 personnel who were recently promoted, Punch reports. Commandant Elijah Willie told the officers to show discipline, integrity and professionalism in their new ranks. The ceremony followed the corps' latest round of promotions for officers serving in the state.

stories.h: Obi pledges 10,000MW of power if elected in 2027
stories.p: NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi asked Nigerians to vote President Tinubu out in 2027, pointing to rising poverty, Punch reports. Obi promised 10,000 megawatts of electricity and an export hub in Aba if he wins. Vanguard quotes him as saying a new Nigeria needs a change of president at the next election.

stories.h: WHO calls for quicker Ebola vaccine trials in DR Congo
stories.p: The World Health Organisation wants Ebola vaccine testing sped up, with the Bundibugyo-strain outbreak in DR Congo now above 12,000 infections, with 5,900 deaths, Punch reports, with insecurity slowing the response. Uganda has begun Africa's first mRNA Ebola vaccine trial with Moderna, while Canada has extended visa curbs on residents of DRC, Uganda and South Sudan by 90 days.

stories.h: Reps panel gets more petitions on poor phone network
stories.p: A House of Representatives panel probing the quality of telecoms services has received a fresh petition against the chief executives of mobile network operators over persistent poor service across Nigeria, New Telegraph reports. The committee also said no arm of government can stop another from carrying out duties the constitution gives it, as it continues its inquiry.

stories.h: States prepare for INEC's Saturday mock accreditation
stories.p: INEC will test its BVAS accreditation devices and IReV result upload in a mock exercise on Saturday, November 28. Ondo says movement will not be restricted during its sanitation exercise so residents can take part, Punch reports. Nasarawa urged people in all 13 councils to join in, Yiaga Africa is sending 347 observers, and Kebbi APC has postponed its campaign launch.

stories.h: 10,000 Imo youths complete Skill-Up digital training
stories.p: About 10,000 young people have completed the fourth round of Imo State's digital empowerment scheme, known as Skill-Up Imo, AIT reports. At the graduation, Governor Hope Uzodimma said his government remains committed to youth development and digital transformation, describing digital skills as key to the future of young people in the state.

stories.h: Oando sets N203.8bn rights issue at N50 a share
stories.p: Oando Plc has signed deals for a rights issue worth about N203.8 billion, priced at N50 per share, as part of its recapitalisation, TVC News reports. On Friday, the day the final terms were announced, buyers sought 26.43 million Oando shares on the NGX but found no sellers, and the stock closed at N39.90, according to Nairametrics.

stories.h: NGX gains N534bn as bank shares rally
stories.p: Nigerian stocks ended the week higher on Friday, November 27, as buying in Zenith Bank and GTCO lifted total market capitalisation of the Nigerian Exchange by N534.17 billion, Nairametrics reports. Investors returned to bank shares in Friday's trading. The rise builds on Thursday's trading, when the market broke a seven-day losing streak.

stories.h: Wike asks Nigerians to back Tinubu's continuity
stories.p: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike on Friday urged Nigerians to support continuity under President Tinubu, saying his economic reforms, including the end of the fuel subsidy, are starting to show results, AIT reports. Addressing a town hall held by the Rainbow Coalition in Degema, Rivers State, Wike said the country should not be handed to politicians he called "gamblers", Leadership adds.

stories.h: Zelensky criticises Trump's friendship with Putin
stories.p: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky told the BBC that Washington is not putting enough pressure on Russia in talks to end the war, and called US President Donald Trump's friendship with Vladimir Putin "strange". Punch reports that Zelensky compared the Russian leader to Hitler. Separately, Al Jazeera says Kyiv has proposed a ceasefire at sea in the Black Sea.

stories.h: Uganda to pull troops out of DR Congo's Lubero
stories.p: Uganda's military announced on Friday that it will withdraw its soldiers from Lubero, a town in North Kivu province in eastern DR Congo, France 24 reports. The move follows a diplomatic row after army chief Muhoozi Kainerugaba threatened to seize Walikale, another town in the province. Ugandan forces have been helping Congo's army fight an Islamist armed group in the region.

stories.h: Real Madrid extend Brahim Díaz deal to 2031
stories.p: Real Madrid have given Morocco forward Brahim Díaz a new contract running until June 2031, Punch reports. His previous deal was due to end in 2027. Díaz, who moved to Madrid from Manchester City in 2019, has won seven trophies with the Spanish club, who are the reigning European champions, according to The Eagle Online.

stories.h: UEFA may punish Marseille after fan violence
stories.p: Marseille face possible UEFA sanctions after fighting in the stands before Thursday's Europa League match with Levski Sofia at the Stade Vélodrome, TVC News reports. France 24 says at least 11 Bulgarian supporters were hurt. French President Emmanuel Macron and Bulgaria's president condemned the violence, and French police have opened an investigation.

stories.h: Culture minister visits Pete Edochie's family in Enugu
stories.p: Culture and Creative Economy Minister Hannatu Musawa visited the Enugu home of the late Nollywood actor Pete Edochie on Friday, November 27, to console his widow, Josephine, and other relatives, PM News reports. Legit.ng says she delivered condolences from President Tinubu. Edochie, one of the best-known faces of Nigerian film, died aged 79.

stories.h: Arteta and Maresca talk up Sunday's Arsenal-City clash
stories.p: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta says his side will not take a struggling Manchester City lightly in Sunday's Premier League meeting at the Emirates, Vanguard reports. Arsenal lead City by six points. City boss Enzo Maresca, whose team have gone 10 games without a clean sheet, said they can win in London, calling the gap between the projects "four months vs seven years".

stories.h: Navy opens seven projects at Onne training school
stories.p: The Nigerian Navy has inaugurated seven new projects at its Basic Training School in Onne, Rivers State, Punch reports. The facilities are meant to ease a shortage of accommodation at the school and to improve the quality of training there. Onne, near Port Harcourt, is home to the navy's main school for new recruits.

stories.h: Lagos families still squeezed by food prices
stories.p: Food costs remain a heavy burden for many Lagos households even though inflation is slowing, Leadership reports. The National Bureau of Statistics said headline inflation eased to 14.06 per cent, down from September's 14.63 per cent, but residents told the paper that prices of staple foods continue to stretch family budgets across the state.

stories.h: Makinde calls for planning and tech-led solutions
stories.p: Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde, the APM's presidential candidate, said Nigeria's problems need strategic planning, smart infrastructure and technology-driven answers, Nigerian Tribune and Blueprint report. Separately, Peoples Gazette says Makinde pledged closer work with the private sector to grow Oyo's exports, naming agriculture, manufacturing and mining as sectors with strong potential.

stories.h: LAWMA promises cleaner Lagos within 60 days
stories.p: Olajuwon Akinyemi, acting head of the state waste agency LAWMA, has promised to improve waste collection across the state and deliver visible change within 30 to 60 days, New Telegraph reports. He warned residents against dumping refuse on highways and public roads. The pledge comes as Lagos called off Saturday's monthly sanitation exercise.

stories.h: Fashola opposes death penalty for election riggers
stories.p: Former Lagos governor Babatunde Fashola said people who rig elections should be jailed rather than executed, Daily Trust reports, urging lawful measures against malpractice ahead of 2027. In separate comments reported by Vanguard, the APC chieftain said Peter Obi's win in Lagos in the 2023 presidential vote "won't happen again", adding the party had not seen the state as a battleground then.

stories.h: Presidency disputes Obi's South Korea salary claim
stories.p: Bayo Onanuga, President Tinubu's adviser on information, said on Friday that Peter Obi's account of Nigeria once paying salaries of South Korean workers under President Shehu Shagari is false, TVC News reports. Writing on X, Onanuga accused the NDC presidential candidate of misrepresenting Nigeria's economic history. The exchange came during a busy week of campaigning for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Kingsley Moghalu to release career memoir
stories.p: Former CBN deputy governor Kingsley Moghalu is set to publish a memoir covering his years at the United Nations, the Central Bank of Nigeria and in party politics, Premium Times reports. Moghalu has written several earlier books, including "Emerging Africa", "Global Justice", "Rwanda's Genocide" and "Build, Innovate and Grow".

stories.h: Abuja chamber sets up five new governing councils
stories.p: The ACCI, Abuja's main business chamber, on Friday inaugurated governing councils for five of its centres of excellence, The Whistler reports. ACCI President Emeka Obegolu told members to focus on accountability, innovation and good service, saying the councils should boost private business growth and better governance in the chamber.

stories.h: Payaza repays N88.94bn commercial paper
stories.p: Payments company Payaza Africa has repaid N88.94 billion owed to investors under its commercial paper programme on the FMDQ Securities Exchange, Nairametrics reports. BusinessDay puts the sum at about KSh 8.5 billion and links the repayment to the firm's new Kenyan licence, as Payaza grows its regulated operations in other African markets.

stories.h: Nigerian journalists honoured at 35th DAME Awards
stories.p: Reporters from several Nigerian newsrooms won prizes at the 35th Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, held in Ikeja, Lagos, on Thursday, November 26. Daily Trust's Afeez Hanafi took the education reporting prize, ICIR's Nurudeen Akewushola won Lagos reporting, and Premium Times journalists won overall best in health reporting and investigations, the outlets report.

stories.h: Farage pledges to end UK Graduate visa route
stories.p: Nigel Farage, leader of Britain's Reform UK party, has promised to scrap the Graduate visa, which allows overseas students to remain and work in the UK after finishing their studies, Punch reports. Nigerians received 20,478 extensions under the route in the 12 months to September 2026, according to figures cited in the report. Reform UK is currently in opposition.

stories.h: Kenya cult leader Mackenzie convicted again
stories.p: A Kenyan court has found preacher Paul Mackenzie guilty of radicalisation and organised crime over a further 123 deaths linked to the Shakahola starvation cult, BBC and Africanews report. The new verdict comes roughly a month after a court gave him a 200-year prison term for killing children in the same case, one of Kenya's worst religious tragedies.

stories.h: Plateau and UNDP train 194 young innovators
stories.p: Plateau State and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) have trained 194 young innovators, Peoples Gazette reports. Speaking at the event, a Mr Nyalun said Plateau drew 2,797 applications, more than any of the other five states taking part in the programme. The 194 participants were picked from that pool of applicants from across the state for the training.

stories.h: Adeleke promises end to Osun council dispute in a week
stories.p: Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke says the long-running dispute over the state's local government councils will be fully settled within one week, Channels TV reports. Speaking as he began his second term in office, Adeleke also said that creating jobs and wealth for residents would be the main focus of his new administration's plans for Osun.

stories.h: INEC says it now has 57,000 BVAS machines for 2027
stories.p: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission has bought 57,000 Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices for the 2027 general elections, The Eagle Online reports. The machines are used to verify voters at polling units and send results for upload. Amupitan gave the figure on Thursday at a civic education seminar hosted by the Anglican Diocese of Abuja.

stories.h: First Lady opens Trans-Warri road and 15 bridges
stories.p: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu on Friday opened 15 bridges and the 20.95km road linking Warri and Ode-Itsekiri, a project of Delta State Governor Sheriff Oborevwori's administration. Speaking in Warri, she said President Bola Tinubu's economic reforms were giving states more money and driving infrastructure projects across Nigeria, New Telegraph and Silverbird TV report.

stories.h: US approves SpaceX plan for one million satellites
stories.p: America's Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's plan to launch one million satellites, Peoples Gazette and Al Jazeera report. Elon Musk welcomed the approval, saying "this will be a great asset to America and the world." Musk wants to place artificial intelligence data centres in space, where almost constant sunshine could supply them with power.

stories.h: FG launches 2026-2030 menstrual health policy
stories.p: The Federal Government has unveiled a five-year national policy, running from 2026 to 2030, on managing menstrual health and hygiene, Voice of Nigeria reports. It was launched in Abuja during the country's second national summit on the issue. Stakeholders at the event urged proper funding, adoption by the states and strong implementation so that women and girls are protected and treated with dignity.

stories.h: Tegbe inspects 480MW Abeokuta power substation
stories.p: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe says reliable electricity is essential if Nigeria is to reach its $1tn economy goal. He spoke on Friday while touring the 480MW New Abeokuta transmission substation in Toolu, Ogun State, which is due for completion in March 2027. FGN Power Company said it has already added 1,080MW of wheeling capacity under the Presidential Power Initiative.

stories.h: Canada's top court backs Quebec religious symbols law
stories.p: Canada's Supreme Court has largely upheld Quebec's secularism law, under which some public employees, among them teachers and police officers, may not wear religious symbols such as hijabs or turbans while on duty. Muslim, Sikh and Catholic teachers were among those who challenged it in court, saying it breached their fundamental rights. Judges found the law mostly constitutional, BBC and Al Jazeera report.

stories.h: Lagos calls week-long ceasefire in Magodo land row
stories.p: The Lagos State Government has directed a one-week ceasefire in the Magodo-Shangisa landlords' dispute, PM News reports. According to a government statement, the state's justice commissioner and Attorney-General, Lawal Pedro, SAN, met stakeholders on Thursday to discuss the disagreement and agree on a peaceful path forward. The truce is meant to give room for a settlement between the parties involved.

stories.h: Fury passes medicals for Anthony Joshua fight
stories.p: Tyson Fury has passed the pre-fight medical checks needed to box Anthony Joshua and is cleared for the bout, Vanguard reports. The clearance follows a row over remarks his wife Paris made about his mental health, which she has since withdrawn. Joshua, the British heavyweight of Nigerian heritage, has a large fan base in Nigeria.

stories.h: Sierra Leone cuts maternal deaths sharply
stories.p: Sierra Leone, once among the riskiest countries for childbirth, has recorded a steep drop in maternal deaths, which Arise News puts at nearly 80%. Wider maternity care and more skilled birth attendants are credited. But Africanews and France 24 report that informal fees, mistrust, weak infrastructure and poor access to emergency care still put mothers at risk.

stories.h: Strong dollar adds pressure on the naira
stories.p: The US Dollar Index has risen to its highest level in 22 months, making it harder for the naira in the foreign exchange market, Nairametrics reports. The outlet links the pressure to heavy local demand for dollars as Christmas and the 2027 general elections approach. The CBN raised its weekly dollar supply to bureaux de change to $1m this week.

stories.h: FG backs 4,000-home cooperative estate in Abuja
stories.p: The Federal Government has given its support to a planned 4,000-unit housing estate in Karshi, Abuja, to be built by the cooperative society CoopEast, Leadership reports. Housing and Urban Development Minister Muttaqah Rabe Darma endorsed the project, which the ministry links to efforts to close Nigeria's housing gap, put at more than 15 million homes.

stories.h: Super Falcons land in Algeria for two friendlies
stories.p: Nigeria's senior women's team is now in Algeria, where the Super Falcons have started preparing for two international friendlies against the host nation's women's side, the Lady Fennecs, Blueprint reports. The matches are part of the team's programme of international games. The Super Falcons are the reigning Women's Africa Cup of Nations champions and record title holders.

stories.h: Pete Edochie had prostate cancer for six years, son says
stories.p: Veteran Nollywood actor Chief Pete Edochie lived with prostate cancer for six years after having surgery abroad, his eldest son Leo Edochie told BBC Pidgin, Punch reports. Tributes continue to come in: Catholic Bishop of Sokoto Matthew Hassan Kukah said the actor's death closes a remarkable era in Nigerian drama and film, Voice of Nigeria reports.

stories.h: Anambra shifts sanitation to Dec 5 for INEC mock test
stories.p: Anambra State has pushed its end-of-year sanitation exercise across the state to December 5 instead of this Saturday, November 28, so residents can join INEC's mock accreditation exercise, Environment Commissioner Clem Aguiyi announced. INEC officials told Punch the commission is ready for Saturday's test in the state, with BVAS devices already set up as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections.

stories.h: Two sentenced to death over 2022 killing of corps member
stories.p: An FCT High Court in Zuba, Abuja, has handed death sentences by hanging to two defendants over the 2022 killing of an NYSC (youth service) member, the FCT Police Command said on Friday. Justice Kezziah Ogbonnaya found them guilty of culpable homicide, an offence that carries the death penalty under the Penal Code. A third defendant received 42 years in prison for his part.

stories.h: Atiku disputes FG's N450bn rice farmers figure
stories.p: Ex-Vice President Atiku Abubakar has dismissed the Federal Government's statement that President Bola Tinubu's administration committed N450bn to rice farmers as propaganda and asked for proof of payment, Daily Post reports. In a statement from his media office on Friday, he also blamed the import of 150,000 tonnes of rice for hurting local mills. Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake cited the figure on Sunday.

stories.h: Guinea-Bissau junta defends delay of December vote
stories.p: Guinea-Bissau's military-led government has defended postponing the elections it had planned for December, Africanews reports. The presidency said the "technical, material, and financial conditions" for a credible vote were not yet in place. Soldiers seized power in the West African country in November 2025, days after a disputed presidential poll, and promised a return to civilian rule.

stories.h: NBMA to check supermarkets for unapproved GMO foods
stories.p: The National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA) says a new surveillance team will inspect supermarkets and shops every two months, Premium Times reports. The visits are meant to confirm that every genetically modified item on Nigerian shelves carries the required approval. The NBMA is the federal body responsible for regulating genetically modified organisms in the country.

stories.h: Suit asks INEC to release Yayi's candidacy papers
stories.p: A resident of Yewa in Ogun State has asked the Abuja division of the Federal High Court to order INEC and the publisher of The Guardian to hand over certified true copies of the documents, credentials and forms of Senator Solomon Adeola (Yayi), the APC governorship candidate, ThisDay and Silverbird TV report. The case is yet to be decided.

stories.h: AFCON 2027: six teams in, Nigeria chase Group L spot
stories.p: Morocco, Senegal, Mali, Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Benin have booked places at the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, Soccernet NG reports. Three qualifying groups still have one ticket each to decide. Nigeria's Super Eagles are competing for the only remaining place in Group L, the group of co-hosts Tanzania.

stories.h: EFCC chief asks justice sector to speed up graft trials
stories.p: EFCC Chairman Ola Olukoyede has asked everyone in the justice sector to cooperate to end delays in corruption prosecutions in Nigerian courts, TVC News reports. He said faster trials need joint effort from the judiciary, the legislature, lawyers, civil society groups and other stakeholders, rather than the anti-graft agency acting alone.

stories.h: FG opens N5m support scheme for 600 tailors
stories.p: The Federal Government has opened applications for a programme that will give 600 Nigerian tailors access to N5m each through a mix of grants and loans to be repaid, Nigerian Tribune and The Eagle Online report. Named the "Business Incubation for Renewed Hope Tailors Programme", the scheme will last five years and the Industrial Training Fund (ITF) is running it.

stories.h: LASEMA: no casualties in GNI House demolition
stories.p: Lagos emergency agency LASEMA says four storeys of the burnt GNI (Great Nigeria Insurance) building on Lagos Island's Martins Street have been pulled down without casualties or serious damage to buildings nearby. The agency rejected reports suggesting otherwise and said the controlled demolition is going on safely, TVC News reports.

stories.h: Ondo Amotekun parades 13 suspects, one tied to 200 break-ins
stories.p: Ondo State's Amotekun Corps on Friday paraded 13 suspects in Akure, among them a man it accuses of breaking into more than 200 homes over six years, The ICIR and Punch report. According to the corps, he copied residents' keys to get into houses in Akure and other towns and sold the stolen goods online. Amotekun says he confessed.

stories.h: Kano governor Yusuf starts 2027 campaign on Sunday
stories.p: Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf will open his 2027 campaign on Sunday and has urged supporters to avoid violence, PM News reports. He said every local government area on the campaign tour would also see new projects commissioned, ongoing ones inspected or foundation stones laid, which he presented as part of his government's delivery to residents.

stories.h: Lagos lawmakers begin review of MDA accounts
stories.p: The Lagos State House of Assembly has started its fourth public accounts review, examining how ministries, departments and agencies spent public money, Punch reports. Lawmakers cautioned the MDAs against irregular and wasteful spending during the exercise. The review is based on the Auditor-General's report for 2025, which covers 210 state bodies, according to reports on the session.

stories.h: Omo-Agege says he did not snub Delta police summons
stories.p: Ovie Omo-Agege, a former Deputy Senate President, has rejected reports that he ignored a request by Delta police to appear over Monday's attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress members at Uduere, Punch and Vanguard report. His camp argued that a summons publicised in the media before reaching him is not due process. He said he would not be tried in the media over the incident.

stories.h: NCTC launches campaign against election violence
stories.p: The National Counter Terrorism Centre, working with the Civil-Military Cooperation Centre, has started a campaign to prevent violence and make the 2027 polls safer, the News Agency of Nigeria and Leadership report. Leadership adds that the Inter Party Advisory Council has recorded deaths from political violence in 26 states.

stories.h: CAF brings VAR to all club group-stage matches
stories.p: The Confederation of African Football will use Video Assistant Referee technology in every group-stage match this season in the CAF Champions League and Confederation Cup, Punch and Blueprint report. The rollout begins with Confederation Cup fixtures on Friday, November 27. The decision covers every group fixture in both CAF club competitions this season.

stories.h: Kano govt denies Yusuf role in EFCC probe of Kwankwaso
stories.p: The Kano State Government has rejected claims by former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso that Governor Abba Yusuf pushed the EFCC to investigate him, Premium Times, Channels TV, Tribune and Vanguard report. The government called the allegation misleading and politically motivated, and said Kwankwaso's EFCC matters started before the current administration. Kwankwaso had accused the governor earlier on Friday.

stories.h: OK Movement group pulls support from Obi and NDC
stories.p: Leaders of the OK Movement say the group has withdrawn its ward, council and state structures from Peter Obi's campaign and the NDC, and is talking to other parties, ThisDay and Vanguard report. Punch describes those behind the move as one faction and says the NDC rejected it, calling them impostors. Accounts of how much of the group is involved differ.

stories.h: Kenyan ex-governor Obado gets 25 years for murder
stories.p: A Kenyan court has sentenced Zacharia Okoth Obado, former governor of Migori County, to 25 years in prison over the killing of a pregnant university student, Nigerian Tribune, Peoples Gazette and Blueprint report. Judges held that Obado provided both the reason and the funds for the killing, which took place while he was in office. Two of his aides were also sentenced.

stories.h: Adamawa to run free buses from December 1
stories.p: Adamawa State Governor Ahmadu Fintiri says the state will offer free bus transport across its local government areas from December 1, 2026, to ease travel costs for residents, TVC News reports. He made the announcement in Guyuk LGA during an APC grassroots campaign event backing President Bola Tinubu. Details of routes and timetables were not given in the report.

stories.h: Fulham boss says Bassey will not be sold in January
stories.p: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa said on Friday that Super Eagles defender Calvin Bassey will not leave the club in the January transfer window, despite reported interest from Manchester United. Speaking before Fulham's match against Bournemouth, Arbeloa praised the Nigerian's leadership and said the club is working on a new contract for him, Complete Sports, Punch and Vanguard report.

stories.h: Dangote refinery shares to list on NGX on Dec 1
stories.p: The Dangote refinery's shares will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange next Tuesday, December 1, according to Business Post. A gong-ringing ceremony to mark the listing is planned at NGX Group House on Customs Street, Marina, Lagos. The listing of Africa's biggest refinery has been widely awaited by investors in Nigeria's stock market.

stories.h: Adeleke begins second term as Osun governor
stories.p: Ademola Adeleke took the oath for a second term as Osun State governor on Friday at the Osogbo City Stadium, with his deputy Kola Adewusi, Daily Trust and Channels TV report. Chief Judge Adepele Ojo administered the oath and Vice President Kashim Shettima attended. Adeleke, re-elected in August on the Accord Party ticket, urged leaders to set aside past differences.

stories.h: Airtel Africa starts new 1% share buyback
stories.p: Airtel Africa Plc has begun another share repurchase programme covering as much as 1% of the shares it has issued, Nairametrics and Premium Times report. Barclays Capital Securities will carry out on-market purchases for the telecom group, which will then acquire the shares from the bank. The move follows completion of the company's previous buyback on November 26.

stories.h: REA signs $20m solar mini-grid deal with Okra
stories.p: The Rural Electrification Agency and solar firm Okra Solar have agreed a $20 million blended-finance deal to expand mesh-grid power to communities with little or no electricity, Nigerian Tribune and Blueprint report. The agreement falls under the agency's MEGA initiative. It aims to speed up deployment of the technology and bring lasting power access to underserved areas across Nigeria.

stories.h: Bolt lowers driver commission to 15%
stories.p: Ride-hailing company Bolt now takes 15% of drivers' fares in Lagos and Abuja, Nairametrics reports, citing a company statement issued on Friday. Before the cut, Lagos drivers paid 20% while Abuja drivers paid 21%. The change could raise what drivers take home as costs of running a car in Nigeria keep climbing.

stories.h: Enugu closes major roads for Tinubu's visit
stories.p: Enugu State will close several major roads from Saturday ahead of President Bola Tinubu's campaign visit to the state, Punch reports. The state government has published alternative routes for motorists and commuters. People travelling in Enugu city this weekend should plan for diversions and possible delays around the routes affected.

stories.h: Adegbuyi is Nigeria's only CAF Awards finalist
stories.p: Flamingos player Adegbuyi has made the final shortlist for the 2026 CAF Awards and is the only Nigerian finalist, Premium Times reports. Flamingos head coach Akeem Busari, who many expected to be nominated, did not make the shortlist for the Women's Coach of the Year award. CAF will name the winners at its awards ceremony.

stories.h: Enugu police rescue kidnapped man, arrest two
stories.p: Enugu State Police Command says officers have rescued a 21-year-old man kidnapped in Abakpa-Nike, Enugu, TVC News and Premium Times report. Police from the Emene division arrested two suspects, aged 21 and 27, after what the command called an intelligence-led operation. The suspects are in custody while the investigation continues.

stories.h: Lagos cancels Saturday sanitation exercise
stories.p: Lagos Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has called off the November environmental sanitation exercise that was due on Saturday, November 28, TVC News reports. The state government said the change avoids a clash with INEC's nationwide mock accreditation and result upload exercise, set for the same day. The government said the move was meant to avoid disrupting the INEC exercise.

stories.h: 2,500 police deployed for Adeleke inauguration
stories.p: Osun State police have deployed 2,500 officers for the second-term inauguration of Governor Ademola Adeleke and his deputy, Kola Adewusi, in Osogbo, Peoples Gazette and Vanguard report. Police promised more patrols and traffic control. Vice-President Kashim Shettima has arrived in Ibadan on his way to represent President Tinubu at the event.

stories.h: UK net migration drops to 77,000
stories.p: Net migration to the United Kingdom fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, the lowest level since 1997 outside the COVID-19 period, Nairametrics and Arise News report. Tighter visa rules and fewer foreign workers and international students drove the fall. Work, study and asylum-related arrivals all declined.

stories.h: Atiku, Obi and Makinde to meet in Abuja Monday
stories.p: Opposition figures Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi and Oyo Governor Seyi Makinde are set to meet in Abuja on Monday ahead of the 2027 elections, Punch reports. The ruling APC said the meeting is no threat to President Tinubu's re-election bid.

stories.h: Defence Minister says he is free to back APC
stories.p: Defence Minister Christopher Musa says he is no longer a military officer and is free to campaign for the ruling APC, Punch and Vanguard report. Musa said he belongs to the APC but that security forces will protect all parties, and he pledged a free and fair 2027 election.

stories.h: PenCom says N40bn unpaid pensions recovered
stories.p: The National Pension Commission has recovered about N40 billion in pension contributions that employers failed to remit for their workers, Director-General Omolola Oloworaran said in an interview reported by Daily Trust. She said current reforms aim to make sure employers pay workers' pension deductions on time. Workers can check their retirement savings accounts to confirm remittances.

stories.h: Senate panel tells gas firms to supply locally first
stories.p: The Senate Committee on Gas Resources has told operators to put the domestic market ahead of LPG exports, Daily Trust reports. Committee chairman Senator Jarigbe Jarigbe said falling supplies of cooking gas to Nigerian buyers could keep prices high across the country. He spoke at a meeting with industry stakeholders in Abuja.

stories.h: Reps bills seek death penalty for fake drug deaths
stories.p: Three bills sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye, chairman of the House Committee on Public Assets, propose at least 20 years in prison for dealing in fake drugs or unsafe processed food, Daily Trust reports. The bills also propose the death penalty where such products are proven to have caused a death. The bills seek to amend existing laws.

stories.h: Five killed in attack on Jigawa village
stories.p: Attackers killed five people and injured six others at Gurjiya village in Aujara District, Jahun Local Government Area of Jigawa State, at about 1am on Wednesday, Daily Trust and Punch report. Residents fled their homes during the attack. It came weeks after a similar attack in the area.

stories.h: Kano health insurance to cover 20,000 mothers, kids
stories.p: Kano State and the National Health Insurance Authority have launched a scheme to cover 20,000 vulnerable women and children under five, Daily Trust reports. The programme, called Mama Pikin – Whole Family Covered, aims to widen access to maternal and child healthcare in the state.

stories.h: Nigeria and Togo seek investors for data parks
stories.p: Nigeria and Togo are looking for private investors to fund a joint data park project worth between $30 million and $50 million, Nairametrics, TechCabal and Peoples Gazette report. The plan is to build one facility in each country to attract international data centre operators and strengthen digital infrastructure across West Africa.

stories.h: Edo Queens open NWFL title defence on Tuesday
stories.p: Defending champions Edo Queens will begin their Nigeria Women Football League title defence against Rivers Angels on Tuesday, December 1, in the opening fixture of the 2026/27 season, the News Agency of Nigeria reports. Edo Queens go into the new campaign as the reigning league champions, with Rivers Angels their first opponents.

stories.h: INEC plans electronic result sheet for 2027 polls
stories.p: INEC says it will use a new electronic result sheet in the 2027 elections to stop differences between results declared at polling units and the figures uploaded to its result viewing portal. The commission says the electronic checks are meant to prevent result manipulation during collation, Premium Times reports.

stories.h: PTAD says FG has cleared pension backlog since 2013
stories.p: The Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) says the Federal Government has cleared unfunded pension liabilities that had built up since 2013. According to PTAD, the lowest-paid pensioner under the old defined benefit scheme now earns N58,000 a month, up from N6,024 in 2024. The directorate gave the figures in a statement reported by Punch.

stories.h: PANDEF asks IGP, DSS to probe Delta rally attacks
stories.p: The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has petitioned the Inspector-General of Police and the DSS to investigate reported killings and attacks on supporters of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The forum says the violence ahead of the 2027 elections is a concern for national security and the economy.

stories.h: Gbajabiamila says IBB backs Tinubu's re-election
stories.p: Chief of Staff Femi Gbajabiamila led a presidential delegation to Minna on Thursday to visit former heads of state Ibrahim Babangida and Abdulsalami Abubakar. In a statement, Gbajabiamila said Babangida backed President Tinubu's re-election bid, while Abdulsalami praised the President's performance and called for peaceful 2027 elections. The visit followed a directive from Tinubu.

stories.h: INEC chairman warns political violence threatens polls
stories.p: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan has raised the alarm over rising political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that attacks on campaign convoys, party supporters and electoral officials could undermine the polls in nine states. He said INEC is working closely with the police and other security agencies to prosecute electoral offenders.

stories.h: ASUU threatens indefinite nationwide strike
stories.p: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) has threatened an indefinite nationwide strike. The union accuses the Federal Government and some state governments of failing to implement key parts of the agreement signed on December 23, 2025, and of leaving salary arrears, allowances and welfare issues of lecturers unpaid and unresolved.

stories.h: Lagos: 119,000 children missed first vaccine dose
stories.p: The Lagos State Government has identified about 119,000 "zero-dose" children who did not receive their first dose of the pentavalent vaccine. The state says it is stepping up immunisation drives and primary healthcare services to reach these children, Punch reports. The figure was released as part of the state's push to improve primary healthcare.

stories.h: Naira gains N19 to N1,378 per dollar
stories.p: The naira gained N19 to close at N1,378 per dollar, Punch reports, after the Central Bank of Nigeria allowed bureau de change operators to buy up to $1m in cash every week. The move is meant to ease seasonal demand for dollars, but the report says the parallel market remains under pressure.

stories.h: Uba Sani says North will back Tinubu in 2027
stories.p: Kaduna Governor Uba Sani says the North has good reasons to vote for President Bola Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 presidential election, citing infrastructure and education spending under the administration. He said every presidential candidate should campaign on his past record, since all leading candidates have held office before, and the era of promises is over.

stories.h: INTERPOL arrests 65 in Mediterranean operation
stories.p: INTERPOL says 65 people were arrested in a major border security operation across 18 countries in Europe, North Africa and the Middle East. The international police organisation said several of those arrested are linked to terrorism investigations. The countries involved lie around the Mediterranean region, TVC News reports.

stories.h: Lagos sanitation exercise holds Saturday Nov 28
stories.p: The Lagos State Government has dismissed rumours that the November monthly environmental sanitation exercise has been postponed. It confirmed that the exercise will hold across the state on Saturday, November 28, 2026. The state confirmed the date after rumours spread that the monthly exercise had been called off.

stories.h: Ramaphosa hosts Obasanjo for infrastructure talks
stories.p: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa has met former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo and a delegation from the Africa Finance Corporation (AFC). Their talks focused on infrastructure development and investment opportunities across Africa, Vanguard reports. The meeting brought together a former Nigerian leader and a major African lender to discuss projects on the continent.

stories.h: NELFUND has paid out N379bn in student loans
stories.p: The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has disbursed about N379 billion after processing around 2.65 million applications, Education Minister Maruf Tunji Alausa has disclosed. Alausa gave the figures on Thursday, TVC News reports, as an update on the student loan scheme run by the Federal Government.

stories.h: India envoy meets Tony Elumelu on business ties
stories.p: India's High Commissioner to Nigeria, Abhishek Singh, met businessman Tony Elumelu and presented him with a plaque. The High Commission said the meeting was about building stronger India–Nigeria partnerships in business, investment and entrepreneurship. Elumelu said he believes entrepreneurship knows no borders, and that his foundation has shown how backing entrepreneurs can create jobs at scale.
stories.cr: Photo: High Commission of India, Abuja

stories.h: CBN names Murtala Mohammed acting Keystone Bank MD
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has appointed Murtala Mohammed as acting managing director and chief executive of Keystone Bank, replacing Hassan Imam, with effect from November 26. CBN spokesman Michael Akuka announced the change on Thursday. The regulator said the bank remains fully operational, with services running normally and customers' funds secure.

stories.h: Trump says he urged Putin to end aggression in Europe
stories.p: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that he had asked Russian President Vladimir Putin to pull back all military aggression in Europe. Punch notes the remark marks a change in tone, coming a week after Trump described the Russian leader as his friend during a visit to China.

stories.h: Prisons hold over 4,000 inmates on death row
stories.p: The Nigerian Correctional Service says more than 4,000 inmates are on death row and that custodial centres across the country are badly congested. The service urged state governors either to commute the death sentences to life imprisonment or to sign the execution warrants, Channels Television reported on Thursday.

stories.h: APC says Tinubu housing schemes built 26,000 homes
stories.p: Housing programmes under President Bola Tinubu have delivered 26,000 units through the Housing Ministry, the Federal Housing Authority and the Federal Mortgage Bank, the APC said on Thursday. Party spokesman Alake added that the schemes created 525,100 construction jobs in three years and that new mortgage measures aim to draw private investment.

stories.h: Navy destroys four illegal refineries in Rivers
stories.p: The Nigerian Navy says it dismantled four illegal refining sites in Rivers State and found about 112,525 litres of suspected stolen crude oil and illegally refined diesel in separate operations. Navy spokesman Captain Abiodun Folorunsho announced the results on Thursday, saying oil thieves keep trying to restart such sites.

stories.h: Free trade zone status for Anambra Industrial City
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has approved free trade zone status for Anambra Industrial City and has also approved two flyovers in Awka, Vice President Kashim Shettima said on Thursday. Shettima made the announcement while inaugurating a newly built flyover at Ekwulobia in Anambra State, Punch reports.

stories.h: NGX ends losing streak as stocks gain N61bn
stories.p: Nigerian stocks rose on Thursday, ending a run of losing sessions on the Nigerian Exchange as investors bought heavyweight energy, banking and financial services shares. Nigerian Tribune put the market's gain at about N61 billion, while the All-Share Index edged up 0.04 per cent, according to Leadership.

stories.h: INEC to test BVAS in 406 Ondo polling units Saturday
stories.p: INEC will hold a mock test of its voter accreditation technology, the BVAS, in Ondo State on Saturday, November 28, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The exercise runs from 8:30am to 2:30pm in 406 polling units across all 18 local government areas of the state, the commission said.

stories.h: Burkina Faso asks Nigeria for help against terrorism
stories.p: Burkina Faso's Security Minister Mahamadou Sana has called for closer security cooperation with Nigeria against terrorism, drug and human trafficking and other cross-border crimes in West Africa. He made the request in Ouagadougou while meeting Nigeria's ambassador, Syndoph Endoni, and cited the Dangote Refinery as an example of Nigeria's industrial progress.

stories.h: Osun NSCDC deploys 1,300 for Adeleke inauguration
stories.p: The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps in Osun State has deployed 1,300 personnel across the state for Governor Ademola Adeleke's second-term inauguration on Friday, November 27. Command spokesperson Adeleke Kehinde said the deployment is meant to protect lives and property and ensure a peaceful ceremony.

stories.h: FG reports 17% drop in maternal deaths in 172 LGAs
stories.p: The Federal Government says maternal deaths have fallen by 17 per cent and newborn deaths by four per cent in 172 local government areas it classes as high-risk for mothers and babies, Nigerian Tribune reported on Thursday. The figures were presented as results of federal maternal and child health interventions in those areas.

stories.h: Ogun police recover baby taken at Ifo market
stories.p: Ogun State Police Command says it has rescued a one-year-old boy who was allegedly snatched from his mother at Ifo Market in August and later sold. Detectives found him in Abeokuta with a couple who reportedly believed they were adopting through a Lagos orphanage. Three female suspects were arrested and the child was reunited with his mother.

stories.h: Aubameyang unhurt after car crash in Spain
stories.p: Gabon striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was not hurt when his Ferrari collided with another car on Spain's AP-9 motorway on Thursday morning while he was driving to Deportivo La Coruña training. He said on Instagram the other driver was fine, and he still trained ahead of this weekend's LaLiga match against Barcelona.

stories.h: NAFDAC shuts Zuba market, seizes N300m fake goods
stories.p: NAFDAC has shut Zuba International Market in the FCT after an enforcement raid in which more than 160 shops were screened and counterfeit and unwholesome products worth over N300 million were seized. The agency said Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye ordered the crackdown to protect consumers from fake goods during the yuletide season.

stories.h: Tinubu gives NAF crash families homes, N100m
stories.p: President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja and N100 million for the families of the 25 people killed in the Nigerian Air Force ATR 42 crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State. He announced the support on Thursday at a memorial and wreath-laying with service chiefs at the National Cemetery in Abuja, Punch reports.

stories.h: Lawal again rules out talks with Zamfara bandits
stories.p: Zamfara Governor Dauda Lawal said on Thursday his government will not negotiate with bandits or their sponsors and will focus on retaking ungoverned areas. He spoke in Gusau at the graduation of 1,000 Zamfara Forest Guards, an armed forest guard scheme launched by President Tinubu in May 2025.

stories.h: CBN lifts BDC weekly dollar cash limit to $1m
stories.p: The Central Bank of Nigeria has temporarily raised the amount of dollar cash licensed Bureau De Change operators can buy each week from $150,000 to $1 million. The change took effect on Wednesday, 25 November, and is meant to ease seasonal demand for foreign currency as the naira weakened past N1,400 per dollar, Business Post reports.
